fields.display_title: Q1: Since you have used Gumbel Sigmoid to optimize the w_i, what is the distribution of all w_i's learnt in the model? Is there any specific loss to force w_i to be close to 0 or 1? What is the performance variance if you need sample the w_i based on Bernouli distributions in the final evaluation?

fields.replying_to: Replying to Customizable Combination of Parameter-Efficient Modules for Multi-Task Learning

fields.display_title: W1: As the adapter in LORA are low-rank linear projection of parameters in attention modules, a combination of task-common and task-specific LORA adapters seems to be equivalent to just Mixture of LORA as addition of linear transformations is still a linear transformation (rows 2 and 3). Thus, it is unclear why decomposing learnable parameters would improve performance.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7467 by Reviewer soi2

fields.display_title: Q1: Could the authors clarify on how they combine different adapters? This would help with understanding as well as reproducibility.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7467 by Reviewer soi2

fields.display_title: W2/Q2: The experimental section misses some studies to show the effective of hyper-parameters in the model; Experiments on the effects of the number of adapters/ranks/tasks could provide better insight on the robustness and limitations of the proposed methods
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7467 by Reviewer soi2

fields.display_title: W3/Q3:The performance seems to saturate when being applied to strong base model such as T5-Large. It seems to suggest that the effect of task-common components vanish when the base model can generalize well toward different downstream tasks; ● Stronger base model can be used to stress-test the generalizability of the proposed framework.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7467 by Reviewer soi2

fields.display_title: W1+W2, Q1+Q4: The method introduces additional hyperparameters like number of common/task-specific skills which may require tuning. It is not clearly analyzed if certain tasks benefit more from common or specialized skills. How is the number of common and task-specific skills determined? Is there a systematic way to set these hyperparameters? Can you provide ablation studies controlling for common vs task-specific skills?
